Index: pom.xml
===================================================================
--- pom.xml	
+++ pom.xml	
@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
+<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
+         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
+         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
+    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>
+
+    <parent>
+        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
+        <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
+        <version>3.3.5</version>
+        <relativePath/>
+    </parent>
+
+    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
+    <artifactId>demo</artifactId>
+    <version>0.0.1-SNAPSHOT</version>
+    <name>demo</name>
+    <description>Spring Boot application with testing support</description>
+
+    <properties>
+        <java.version>17</java.version>
+    </properties>
+
+    <dependencies>
+        <dependency>
+            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
+            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter</artifactId>
+        </dependency>
+
+        <dependency>
+            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
+            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
+            <scope>test</scope>
+        </dependency>
+    </dependencies>
+
+    <build>
+        <plugins>
+            <plugin>
+                <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
+                <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
+            </plugin>
+        </plugins>
+    </build>
+
+</project>

parts.text:
No Java/Maven available. The task is to set up a new Maven Spring Boot Java project. I'll create the scaffolding files. Since no Java/Maven available, I can't verify by building, but I can create a correct project.

Let me create a standard Spring Boot Maven project. The testing dependencies:
- spring-boot-starter-test (includes JUnit 5, Mockito, AssertJ, Spring Test, etc.)

I should create:
- pom.xml
- src/main/java/.../Application.java
- src/main/resources/application.properties
- src/test/java/.../ApplicationTests.java

Let me pick a package name. Default maybe com.example.demo. Let me create.

Should I use spring initializr? No internet maybe. Let me just write files.

Let me choose Spring Boot 3.3.x (latest around 2026 maybe 3.4/3.5). Given date Sept 2026, Spring Boot 3.5.x likely. But safest known version. I'll use 3.3.4 or 3.4.x. Let me use a recent stable. Since I can't verify, I'll pick 3.3.4 which is well established. Actually by Sept 2026, 3.3 is EOL maybe. But it's fine. Could use 3.4.1. Let me use 3.3.5.

Java version 17.

The "testing support - mocking, assertions, and loading Spring context" maps to spring-boot-starter-test. Mocking = Mockito, assertions = AssertJ/JUnit, loading context = @SpringBootTest. Let me demonstrate in a test.

Let me create files.

input.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
        <version>3.3.5</version>
        <relativePath/>
    </parent>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>demo</artifactId>
    <version>0.0.1-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <name>demo</name>
    <description>Spring Boot application with testing support</description>

    <properties>
        <java.version>17</java.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter</artifactId>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
                <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>

</project>

Actually simpler: just the context test plus one test showing mocking + assertions. Let me create a simple service and its unit test.

I'll keep it focused: create GreetingService and GreetingRepository? Let's do a service that uses a Clock or a repository. Simpler: GreetingService depends on a MessageRepository interface. Then test with Mockito @Mock.

Let me create.

Now the tests. Two test classes:
1. DemoApplicationTests - loads Spring context (@SpringBootTest), assertions.
2. GreetingServiceTest - pure Mockito mocking + AssertJ assertions.

Also application.properties. And .gitignore.

Now let me verify structure. No maven to build. Let me try to install maven? Probably no network. I'll just verify files exist. Let me give a summary.

Actually I should double check the pom for correctness. `spring-boot-starter-test` brings JUnit 5, Mockito, AssertJ, Spring Test, JSONassert, Hamcrest. Good.

I could try downloading maven but no network likely. Let me quickly check if network available via mvnw generation? Not necessary. Let me just do a final listing.

Created a Spring Boot 3.3.5 / Java 17 Maven project at `/work`:

- `pom.xml` — `spring-boot-starter-parent`, `spring-boot-starter`, and `spring-boot-starter-test` (provides JUnit 5, Mockito, AssertJ, Spring Test).
- `DemoApplication.java` + a small `GreetingService`/`MessageRepository` example.
- `GreetingServiceTest.java` — Mockito mocking (`@Mock`, `@InjectMocks`, BDD) with AssertJ assertions.
- `DemoApplicationTests.java` — `@SpringBootTest` context loading with AssertJ assertions.
- `.gitignore`, `application.properties`.

Note: Java/Maven aren't installed here, so I couldn't run `mvn test`. Once available: `mvn test`.
